AGENDA
  GLENDALE WATER AND POWER COMMISSION
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) COUNCIL CHAMBER
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water and Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast
 live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for
 program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office.
 Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
 https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If you have any question about
 matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Glendale Water & Power
 Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Glendale Water & Power Administration Office,
 141 N. Glendale Ave., Suite 450, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  JUNE 7, 2021 AT 4:00 PM

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale Water and Power Commission meeting will be
available to the public electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

  1
 For public comments and questions during the meeting call (818) 937-8100.

City staff will be submitting these questions and comments in real time to the appropriate person
during the Glendale Water and Power Commission meeting.

1.  ROLL CALL – 4:00 PM
2.  GWP COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
3.  REPORTS - INFORMATION
  a. Legislative Update
  b. Renewable Portfolio Update
4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (5) Minutes
  Discussion is limited to items NOT part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5)
  minutes – Commission may question or respond to the speaker, but there will be no debate or
  decision. The General Manager may refer the matter to appropriate staff for investigation and
  report.
5.  AGENDA FORECAST
6.  ADJOURNMENT

MINUTES
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  CITY HALL - COUNCIL CHAMBER
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206

  Monday, June 07, 2021, 4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:02 p.m.

  Present: President Flanigan, Commissioners Jazmadarian, Kedikian, Lall, and Peterson

2. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  Commissioners Kedikian and Peterson expressed their joy in being back to doing ‘in-person’
  meetings. President Flanigan commented on his concerns regarding ransomware and hackers
  going after critical electrical infrastructure. Interim General Manager of GWP, John Takhtalian,
  assured the Commission that the City is actively addressing cybersecurity risks, including
  training and testing to prevent cyber-attacks, phishing, etc.

3. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Legislative Update
  Mr. Leo Zalyan, Administrative Analyst/Legislative Affairs, provided information relating to
  the 2021 legislative calendar. He stated that June 4, 2021, is the last day for bills to pass
  from their house of origin, and on June 15th, the budget bill must be passed by midnight.
  Mr. Zalyan provided highlights from the state budget and summarized key energy and water
  bills. Mr. Zalyan addressed a question by Commissioner Lall in regards to the total
  arrearages (utility delinquencies) per the Governor’s proposal. Commissioner Peterson
  asked if both the Senate Pro Tem Proposal and the Governor proposal go for a vote (State
  Budget), and Mr. Zalyan responded that both parties are negotiating to come up with a
  compromise proposal to pass for the June 15th deadline.

  b. Renewable Portfolio Update
  Ms. Chie Valdez, Power Planning Manager, provided the regulatory background and
  framework for the Renewables Portfolio Standard (RPS) Program, which was established in
  2002, managed by the California Energy Commission, and based on the percentage of
  retail electricity sales served by renewable resources. Ms. Valdez compared the RPS
  Compliance Periods under Senate Bill (SB 100) and SB350 and noted that the renewables
  target has increased from 50% to 60% under SB 100. She discussed GWP's recently
  submitted 2020 Power Source Disclosure, where the City increased the renewable content
  of its portfolio by four percent. Ms. Valdez described GWP's existing and proposed
  renewable and clean energy resources, explained mitigation and compliance strategies for
  meeting RPS and clean energy requirements, and expressed the risk and concerns of not
  meeting such requirements.

  1
   Ms. Valdez discussed the 100% Clean Energy by 2030 feasibility study and highlighted
  potential future clean resources beneficial to GWP, such as renewable natural gas, Green
  Hydrogen, and long-duration storage.

  Ms. Valdez and City staff responded to the Commissioners' questions regarding
  transmission capacity for additional renewable projects, the ten-year contract duration
  requirement for renewables, GWP capacity to serve load, the technologies discussed in the
  Ascend report and offshore wind technology. Commissioner Kedikian suggested an annual
  Clean Energy beyond 2030 report.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Herbert Molano (request for a CIP assessment for electric and water)

5. AGENDA FORECAST
  The Commissioners reviewed and approved the agenda for the August 2021 meeting with the
  following changes:

  August 2, 2021: Update on EIR Evaluation (and the possibility of having a Special Commission
  Meeting in September to further discuss the EIR Evaluation).

6. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Seconded by: Commissioner Lall
  Motion Passed.

  The meeting was adjourned at 5:14 p.m.
